title: Open Call for Consultants – Health Policy Advocacy and Communications
description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here

PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.

Open Call for Consultants - Health Policy Advocacy and Communications

Working across our portfolio PATH 's Center for Advocacy & Policy turns evidence into policy adoption and sustainable financing. We partner with governments, regional bodies, and multilateral institutions to strengthen the evidence, relationships, and policy processes that inform decisions on budgets, regulation, and health system priorities helping accelerate access to proven health innovations. As our portfolio grows across sub-Saharan Africa, donor capitals, and multilateral forums, we are building a roster of experienced consultants and specialist organizations to provide surge capacity for defined, time-bound assignments.

Scopes of Work
Selected consultants will be engaged on a project-by-project basis and may support a range of activities, including:

• Political economy literacy and analysis, stakeholder mapping, and influence strategy in specific countries or regional bodies

• Advocacy campaign design and delivery - theory of change, power mapping, message and narrative strategy, moment planning, and coalition mobilization to secure specific policy or financing decisions

• Development of advocacy tools including policy briefs, positioning papers, technical reports, and presentations

• Health financing and public financial management analysis - budget cycle engagement, domestic resource mobilization, investment cases, and debt-and-fiscal-space framing

• Rapid evidence synthesis - ability to surface relevant research quickly and distill it into decision-relevant form

• Data visualization and storytelling - making complex data intuitive and politically compelling

• Government relations.

• Technical policy engagement with ministries of health, finance, and national regulatory authorities

• Regional and continental advocacy support (African Union, Africa CDC, AUDA NEPAD, African Medicines Agency) and multilateral engagement (WHO governing bodies, Global Fund, Gavi, Unitaid)

• Development of advocacy communications products - media strategy, op-ed and press material development, polling and public opinion research, and launch packages

• Facilitation and convening - designing and running iterative collaborative processes with diverse actors (government officials, donors, civil society, researchers); managing group dynamics across power asymmetries

• Event management - design and delivery for high-level global and regional moments and events

• Advocacy and funding proposal development - articulating theory of change and translating advocacy strategy into competitive proposals for philanthropic, bilateral, and multilateral donors

Qualifications
We are seeking candidates who meet all of the following core requirements:
Core Requirements

• Demonstrated experience in health policy, advocacy, or government engagement in low- and middle-income, and multilateral settings

• Fluency in English

• Strong client-facing communication and facilitation skills

• Ability to work independently in dynamic, multicultural, and politically sensitive environments

• Project management skills
Desirables

• Degree in public policy, public health, economics, international development, or equivalent experience

• Demonstrated experience designing and running advocacy or political campaigns that achieved a defined change in government policy, budget, or public commitment - including coalition-building, grassroots or grasstops mobilization, and narrative strategy

• Systems thinking and problem mapping - ability to diagnose complex policy problems, map stakeholder incentives, and identify

title: Software Engineer, Agentic AI
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics 

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,  we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform - best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics 

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation.  Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together. 

What do we need

We are looking for an experienced and highly skilled Software Engineer (Agentic AI), to build the AI agent at the core of Dotmatics Luma platform. You will own the agent end to end: how it reasons, which tools it uses, what it remembers, how it recovers from failure, and how we know it is working. You will work in a small, high-trust engineering team alongside Product, scientists, and the wider Dotmatics organisation.

This is also an AI-native engineering role. Your success won’t be measured by how many lines of code you write. It will come from how well you decompose work for coding agents, give them the right context, tools, and constraints, verify their output with tests and review, and ship production software faster than a traditional senior engineer without lowering the quality bar. Coding agents are your default path for implementation, and you stay accountable for architecture, correctness, security, and review.

We want someone who thinks like the engineers who build frontier AI products: rigorous about quality, curious about how agents fail, and quick to adapt as models improve. You use AI tools daily to build AI tools, and you ship agents that work in production, not just in demos.

In this role you will get to

• Develop the agent itself: the loop, harness, and control flow connecting the model, tools, and state, including subagents, long-running tasks, checkpointing, and recovery.

• Practice context engineering: decide what goes into the context window, when to compact or summarize, and how to keep the agent coherent over long-running experiments.

• Design tools for the agent, with clear interfaces and descriptions, covering instrument orchestration, scheduling, data capture, and developer tooling such as GitHub, repositories, CI/CD, and workflows.

• Give the agent memory and state persistence so it learns from and builds on earlier work.

Si estás listo para crecer y liderar tu camino, ¡Flix es el lugar para ti!

title: In-Home Physician Full Time - Cleveland
description:
Job Title: In-Home Physician Full Time - Cleveland
Job Location: Work at Home, Ohio, United States
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Full time
Job Seniority Level:
We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD
Full-time employees qualify for our comprehensive benefits package, including:

• Health, dental and vision insurance

• Paid time off

• Annual CEU allowance

• 401K

• Supplies and other perks

• Malpractice coverage

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

Anticipated Weekly Hours
40 Time Type
Full time Pay Range

Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Per Diem Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
"I love seeing health plan members at home. You get a better picture of their health when you see where they live.” - Erica R., PA
“At Signify Health, we have the time to help people and to truly listen to their questions and concerns. We can help guide them so they can take better care of themselves. We really can make a change in communities.” - Ali B., NP
“I like how Signify Health manages my experience. I’m just doing the clinician part of my job without all the administrative responsibilities. I have the time to provide education so people have a better understanding of their health. I can answer their questions without rushing out the door.” - Andrew K., PA

• Hourly base rate, plus additional incentive structure (i.e., per visit completed, other incentives may apply)

• Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

• Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (NPs and PAs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Board certification (required)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

The anchor competency for this role is support scaling. title: VP, Business Development and Earned Revenue
description:
Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.
Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.
With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.
At Code for America , you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts.
Code for America is looking for a talented VP of Business Development and Earned Revenue who will establish evidence-backed earned-revenue models that advance Code for America 's mission and contribute to its long-term financial sustainability. Impact will include paying customers, viable delivery economics, disciplined investment decisions, and a practical path to growing the strongest offerings.
About the role:
The VP of Business Development and Earned Revenue will build and prove Code for America ’s earned-revenue strategy, from identifying promising business models to testing them with paying customers and growing what works. Code for America is a nonprofit with an approximately $40 million annual budget, funded primarily through philanthropy. This leader will identify which mission-aligned offerings, buyers, and business models can strengthen that funding base, test them with paying customers, and guide decisions about where to invest and grow.
This is a hands-on executive role for someone who has built a new line of business from an uncertain starting point. Working with the CEO and across Product, Programs, Engineering, and Finance, the VP will translate ideas into focused commercial experiments, personally secure early paid engagements, and turn the strongest opportunities into repeatable offerings. Those offerings may include products, standardized services, implementation support, or a combination. As a member of the executive leadership team, the VP owns Code for America ’s earned-revenue strategy, makes portfolio decisions within an agreed investment threshold, and brings larger investment decisions to the CEO and Board. The VP leads in a matrixed environment, partnering with Delivery and Enablement teams.
The Strategic Partnerships team will continue to own ongoing government partnership development within Code for America 's existing strategy. The VP will collaborate with that team when testing paid government offerings. Ownership of government buyer relationships, commercial testing, and customer commitments will be defined in a shared agreement with Strategic Partnerships leadership before outreach begins.
Specific revenue and learning targets will be agreed with the CEO. Success in the first year will include:

• A prioritized earned-revenue strategy grounded in customer discovery, mission value, and business cases with explicit assumptions.

• A small number of paid tests that generate revenue and credible evidence about buyer demand, pricing, procurement, and delivery economics.

• Clear recommendations - made in close partnership with the CEO - about which models deserve further investment, which need refinement, and which should stop, with a practical growth and staffing plan for the strongest opportunities.

This role will report to the CEO and is expected to travel no more than 25 % of the time.

title: Technical Instructional Designer (AI Programmes)
description:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. AI can draft a lesson in seconds. It can't tell you whether that lesson will actually land with a nervous career-switcher three weeks into a Data or AI apprenticeship - or whether the concept it just explained is subtly, but fundamentally, flawed.

That's where you come in.

You'll be the human judgement layer sitting on top of our AI-assisted content pipeline - part subject-matter expert, part instructional designer. You'll decide what AI got right, fix what it didn't, and build the parts no AI can: the high-touch, high-stakes, deeply human moments in a learner's journey that make the difference between content that's technically correct and content that actually changes someone's career.

You'll have experience building content in generative and agentic AI, Data Analytics, and Data Science - not just someone who's read about it, but someone who can explain it, question it, and know when the AI-generated explanation of a neural network is actually going to help a learner or quietly confuse them.

Apply end-to-end backward design to build Data and AI programmes where success is measured by what learners can do on the job - not just what they can pass a test on. You'll own the hardest part: turning a job-aligned outcome into a curriculum that actually gets learners there.

- Chase real-world impact, relentlessly. When a piece of learning isn't landing - when a Data Analyst cohort isn't showing the outcomes it should - you won't wait to be told. You'll spot it, own it, and scope the revisions that bring it up to the standard it needs to hit.

- Build what AI can't. Design the custom, high-touch programmes and creative assets - branching narratives, bespoke multimedia, high-stakes onboarding moments - that need real human empathy, creativity, and nuance. If AI could've built it, it's not your job; if only a person could, it is.

- Put AI to work, deliberately. Use AI tools and prompt engineering to accelerate your own content development and uncover learning design approaches nobody's tried yet. This isn't about using AI because it's there - it's about knowing exactly where it earns its place.

- Advise up, not just build. Work directly with Programme Designers and senior stakeholders on the quality and pedagogical effectiveness of AI and human output. Your feedback doesn't stay in the room - it shapes how our AI rules and frameworks evolve.

- Prototype for the long game. Lead new learning formats and modalities that don't exist yet - and know how to balance shipping fast against building something sustainable enough to reuse.

title: User Education Lead

About the team

Customer Education helps people and organizations build the skills and confidence to use AI effectively. We create courses, live learning, community programs and product education that help people apply OpenAI’s products to their work.

About the role

We’re looking for a User Education Lead who is excited about what AI can make possible for people at work and wants to bring more people along on that journey.

You’ll lead education for enterprise users who are getting started with AI or need help turning early experimentation into everyday use. You’ll help people discover what’s possible, build confidence through practice and develop the judgment to use AI well.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves both building and teaching. You’ll explore new products, work directly with learners, create practical education and test what helps people make progress. You’ll develop role-based learning and new approaches to teaching AI, then turn what works into frameworks and resources that can reach more people.

You’ll work closely with teams across Customer Education, Product and go-to-market to connect this foundational learning to the broader customer experience and help learners progress as their skills grow.

In this role, you will:

- Own the education roadmap for people getting started with AI at work. Identify the skills they need, where they get stuck and the opportunities to help them make meaningful progress.

- Build and deliver role-based learning. Create courses, live sessions, demonstrations and exercises grounded in the work people actually do, helping learners apply AI to useful tasks in their own roles.

- Develop and test new approaches to AI education. Experiment with how concepts are explained, how practice is structured and how learners are supported. Turn what works into frameworks and resources that others can adapt and use.

- Help people build lasting skills and confidence. Design learning that helps people move from a first useful experience to independent, repeat use, with clear paths into more advanced education.

- Stay close to the product and the learner. Explore new capabilities firsthand, listen to customers and work with Product and customer-facing teams to keep education relevant as their needs change.

- Measure and improve your work. Assess whether people are developing skills and applying what they learn, then use those insights to improve the learning experience and guide future investment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have built and led education programs that help people develop practical skills and change how they work.

- Are an engaging teacher and clear writer who can make complex ideas accessible and exciting without oversimplifying them.

- Are energized by AI’s potential for workers and curious about how to help people who are uncertain, skeptical or just getting started.

- Use AI actively in your own work, test what you teach and can explain both where it helps and where human judgment matters.

- Love finding better ways to teach. You listen to learners, try new approaches, learn from the results and share what works.

- Can set a focused direction, build strong partnerships and deliver high-quality work as products and customer needs evolve.

Nice to have:

- Experience designing learning for different professional roles or functions.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. title: IT Solutions Analyst
description:
IT Solution Analyst
Position Summary
Random Bit is seeking an IT Solution Analyst to support enterprise architecture, technology modernization, and architecture governance initiatives. This is not a traditional business process or requirements-only analyst role. The position works at the intersection of business and technology, with an emphasis on capability modeling, architecture analysis, requirements traceability, solution planning, and architecture decision support.
The successful candidate will be able to structure complex or ambiguous problems, collaborate across business and technical teams, and translate analysis into clear, decision-ready recommendations and work products.
Key Responsibilities

• Elicit, analyze, document, and validate business, technical, non-functional, and architecturally significant requirements.

• Analyze current-state processes, capabilities, systems, applications, technologies, and integrations to identify gaps, risks, dependencies, and improvement opportunities.

• Develop and maintain business and technical capability models and map capabilities to business outcomes, requirements, enterprise standards, systems, and modernization initiatives.

• Establish and maintain traceability among business needs, capabilities, requirements, architecture standards, decisions, and solution components.

• Support the development of current-state and future-state architecture views, solution plans, assessments, process flows, system diagrams, and related architecture artifacts.

• Contribute to enterprise architecture standards, principles, procedures, and governance processes, including materials for architecture reviews and decisions.

• Conduct research, gap analysis, impact analysis, and alternatives analysis and develop evidence-based recommendations.

• Facilitate stakeholder discussions and collaborate with architects, technical specialists, business stakeholders, project leaders, and vendors to resolve questions and advance work toward decisions.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• Five or more years of experience in business analysis, systems analysis, enterprise analysis, technology consulting, solution planning, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated experience eliciting, analyzing, documenting, and managing complex business and technical requirements.

• Experience performing current-state, future-state, gap, impact, or alternatives analysis.

• Experience establishing traceability among business needs, requirements, processes, systems, capabilities, or solution components.

• Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and develop clear, evidence-based conclusions and recommendations.

• Excellent analytical, critical-thinking, facilitation, and written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate with both business and technical audiences.

• Experience working with cross-functional teams in Agile or iterative delivery environments and using tools such as Jira and Microsoft 365.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting enterprise, business, solution, application, data, or technology architecture initiatives.

The programme
An established organisation is automating its finance operations on Redwood Finance Automation. The work covers the record-to-report cycle: the period-end close, account reconciliation, journal processing and the reporting that follows, all connected to the organisation's ERP.
You will build what the solution design sets out. You will configure the close and reconciliation processes, build the integrations with the ERP and the systems around it, and carry each process through testing, go-live and early support.
What you will work on
Close processes built and configured end to end: task lists, dependencies, approvals and the automated steps between them. Automated account reconciliation, including matching rules and exception handling. Journal entry automation, from data preparation and validation through to posting in the ERP. Integration with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and other source systems, through standard connectors, file and API interfaces. Intercompany, accrual and reclassification steps automated alongside the close. Workflow logic in REL or JavaScript where the standard designer does not meet the requirement. Unit and integration testing, defect fixing, and support through user acceptance testing. Promotion between environments, cutover and hypercare. Technical documentation and handover to the support team.
What you bring
Hands-on delivery on Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance), where you built close, reconciliation or journal processes yourself on at least one live implementation. 5 or more years in finance systems or automation engineering. Working knowledge of SAP FI/CO postings and master data, or the Oracle equivalent, and where ERP integrations tend to break. Workflow scripting in REL or JavaScript, and hands-on ERP integration. A finance-side understanding of the record-to-report cycle and month-end controls.
Useful but not essential:
Redwood RunMyJobs workload automation. BlackLine, Trintech, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. A current Redwood certification. Financial services or another regulated industry, including work under SOX or similar audit controls.
How to respond
Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood implementation: the finance processes in scope, the ERP it connected to, and what you built yourself.

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood Finance Automation people in front of the client.

You will hire and grow a high-performing team, set the strategy and roadmap for vulnerability management from code to cloud, and make secure-by-default the easiest path for every developer. TEAM LEADERSHIP & STRATEGY

- Build, lead, and mentor a team of cloud security, infrastructure vulnerability management, and application security engineers; own hiring, career development, and performance management.

- Work with Compliance/GRC to produce audit-ready evidence of remediation timeliness, and lead the security side of external audits for vulnerability management controls.

- Track and report metrics such as SLA attainment, mean time to remediate, backlog age, and exceptions, by team and severity.

- Secure critical SaaS platforms with sound configurations, access controls, and integrations.

title: Data Platform Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

At ClickHouse, we believe in making product decisions grounded in data, not gut feelings. To support that, we've built a comprehensive internal data warehouse - read more about it on our blog https://clickhouse.com/blog/building-a-data-warehouse-with-clickhouse. It powers analytics, forecasting, and decision-making across every team in the company.

Our stack centers on ClickHouse as the core storage and processing engine, complemented by dbt, Airflow, S3, AWS, Superset, and GitHub Actions. We ingest data from 30+ distinct external sources, process over 2.5 PB of data, and deliver most data marts to business consumers with a 1-hour end-to-end latency - a standard that demands highly optimized, rock-solid transformation pipelines.

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer to help evolve the DWH platform, push its technical boundaries, and deliver reliable, high-performance data models to business users across the organization.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. DWH Platform Development

- Design and develop reusable Airflow components - operators, connectors, and hooks - along with custom integrations tailored to our data architecture.

- Build reusable dbt macros and abstractions: incremental strategies, ETL building blocks, and generic data quality tests, all optimized for ClickHouse-specific behavior and our data patterns.

- Develop DataOps tooling - CI pipelines, data migration frameworks, and security controls - with a strong focus on reliability, self-service usability, and scale.

2. Team contributions

- Conduct thorough code reviews for team members and other team contributors.

- Actively participate in technical and architectural design discussions.

- Drive technical leadership in specific areas of our stack.

- Continuously improve the team's development environment, with a focus on automation - including AI-assisted workflows.

- Contribute to platform stability through proactive troubleshooting and timely incident resolution.

3. Data modeling

- Develop, refactor, and optimize business data models in line with our modeling standards and ClickHouse best practices.

- Mentor and support contributors through code reviews and technical guidance.

- Lead the design and implementation of the most technically demanding data marts - particularly those involving high data velocity, large volumes, or complex business logic.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

- Exceptional SQL skills - this is non-negotiable.

- Strong hands-on experience with Airflow, dbt, and Python.

- Proven track record building and optimizing large-scale, high-throughput data pipelines.

- Solid understanding of data warehousing fundamentals: ETL/ELT, dimensional modeling, and data quality.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

- Comfortable thriving in a fast-paced startup environment - exciting and dynamic, but sometimes wonderfully chaotic.

Preferred:

- Hands-on experience with ClickHouse - a significant advantage.

- Familiarity with AWS or other cloud platforms.

- Experience with CI/CD development, especially using GitHub Actions.

PERKS

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

- Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

- Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

- A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

- Global Gatherings - We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

CULTURE - WE ALL SHAPE IT

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.
